data.narrative:
PILGRIM is a Seed-stage defense and security technology company founded by Jake Adler that has raised $4.3M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 10 private and 2 public companies operating in the Defense & Security sector, including peers such as UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Castelion.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-Progression modeling uses the $4.3M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression, implying a valuation of $11M. Peer-Median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—UFORCE (Seed, $1.0B), Singularity (Series A, $400M), and NODA AI (Series A, $125M)—yielding a median implied valuation of $400M and a range spanning $125M to $1.0B.

The triangulated analysis produces a range of $9M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $205M. The wide dispersion reflects fundamental uncertainty in applying peer multiples to an early-stage company; UFORCE's $1.0B valuation at Seed stage creates significant upside sensitivity, while stage-progression conservatism anchors the lower bound. Key uncertainties include PILGRIM's relative technology differentiation, customer traction beyond capital raised, and the extent to which the defense sector's current market conditions justify the elevated valuations observed in peer Seed and Series A rounds.
